blocks.text: The module documentation explains the device credential, its two storage backends, fail-closed file checks, and the rule that secrets must not appear in output or tracebacks.
blocks.title: Credential storage contract

blocks.text: AuthError and its subclasses distinguish retryable network/server failures, protocol and login outcomes, revocation, server mismatch, and storage safety failures.
blocks.title: Authentication error vocabulary

blocks.text: Secret exposes its value only through reveal while redacting string representations and refusing mutation and pickling. Credential validates the wrapped secret, device UUID, and normalized server URL.
blocks.title: Redacted values and credentials

blocks.text: The path and keyring username are derived from the configured profile. Keyring loading is lazy and unusable backends are treated as unavailable; read failures do not hide a file credential.
blocks.title: Backend locations and optional keyring

blocks.text: Credentials are serialized into a Secret-wrapped JSON payload. Parsing catches all malformed-input failures and returns None so secret-bearing locals do not remain on an exception traceback.
blocks.title: Payload conversion

blocks.text: Saving uses a same-directory temporary file, mode 0600, flush and fsync, then atomic replacement. Reading checks file identity, ownership, regular-file status, permissions, bounded size, and UTF-8 content.
blocks.title: Private credential file I/O

blocks.text: save_credential writes to keyring when possible and removes the file copy, otherwise writes the file and forgets stale keyring data. load_credential prefers keyring then validates file data; delete_credential removes both backends.
blocks.title: Public credential lifecycle

gotchas: The keyring is optional and a broken keyring falls back to the file.
Loading refuses insecure files instead of tightening them.
Deletion is more forgiving than loading so logout can clean up unsafe files.
how_it_works: Validates credential identity and server URL
Reads or writes keyring and file backends
Converts malformed or unsafe storage into fixed AuthError messages
purpose: This module defines authentication errors and the credential record used by login and the device link. It prefers a usable OS keyring and otherwise uses a private atomically written file, with fail-closed checks for ownership, permissions, symlinks, size, and payload shape.
summary: Stores, validates, loads, and deletes the device credential without exposing its secret.
